messages.subject: bug in geom_errorbar()
parts:
Hi all,

I've found a bug in geom_errorbar() and would like to report here.
A very simple reproducible code is as follows.

> ggplot(data=data.frame(x=c(1:10),y=c(1:10),e=c(1:10)), aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymax=y+e/2, ymin=y-e/2)) + ylim(0,6)

If you plot without ylim option, then it works fine. With the ylim option, however,
the vertical bars do not appear properly when ymax or ymin is out of the y range;
in this example the data points at x larger than 4 do not have vertical lines that
should be shown up.

Moreover, there is a similar bug in using xlim. The horizontal lines at both the
end points of the vertical line do not show up correctly when a part of the horizontal
lines is out of xlim. For example,

> ggplot(data=data.frame(x=c(1:10),y=c(1:10),e=c(1:10)), aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymax=y+e/2, ymin=y-e/2)) + xlim(0.5,4.2)

this does not show the data at x=4 properly.

Best,
JJ


Jongjeong Kim

parts:
Were you expecting this?

p <- ggplot(data=data.frame(x=c(1:10),y=c(1:10),e=c(1:10)), aes(x=x,y=y)) +
geom_point() +
geom_errorbar(aes(ymax=y+e/2, ymin=y-e/2))
p + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 6))

Dennis
